{"passages":[{"reference":"6","text":"For if you become occupied with the cares of ordinary life, you will lay a snare both for yourself and for your hearers. For because your occupations leave you unable to equip them with what is beneficial, you will be punished for not teaching what is beneficial, while those who did not learn will perish, ignorance being the cause. Therefore, give them your undistracted time and preside over them, so that at the right time you may provide words capable of saving them. And so let them heed you, knowing that whatever the ambassador of the truth binds on earth has also been bound in heaven, and whatever he looses has been loosed. You, however, will bind what must be bound and loose what must be loosed. These, then, and things like them are the duties that concern you as the presiding officer.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"βιωτικαῖς μερίμναις ἀσχοληθῇς","chosen":"become occupied with the cares of ordinary life","rationale":"βιωτικός concerns everyday worldly life, while ἀσχολέομαι emphasizes being occupied and deprived of leisure."},{"source_quote":"τὰ συμφέροντα ἐφοδιάζειν","chosen":"equip them with what is beneficial","rationale":"ἐφοδιάζω depicts supplying provisions or equipment; the hearers are the implied recipients."},{"source_quote":"εὐσχολῶν προκαθέσθητι","chosen":"give them your undistracted time and preside over them","rationale":"εὐσχολέω contrasts with prior preoccupation, while προκαθέζομαι denotes taking the leading or presiding position."},{"source_quote":"ὁ τῆς ἀληθείας πρεσβευτὴς","chosen":"the ambassador of the truth","rationale":"πρεσβευτής denotes an authorized envoy or ambassador, not merely an elder."},{"source_quote":"δέδεται καὶ ἐν οὐρανῷ","chosen":"has also been bound in heaven","rationale":"The Greek perfect is retained rather than harmonized with a familiar future-tense biblical rendering."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οἱ δὲ μὴ μαθόντες ἀγνοίας αἰτία ἀπολοῦνται","issue":"The printed nominative αἰτία is syntactically abrupt. It can be understood parenthetically, “ignorance being the cause,” as translated, though a dative expressing cause is a possible conjecture.","proposed_reading":"οἱ δὲ μὴ μαθόντες ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ ἀπολοῦνται","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ τὰ μὲν. κατὰ σὲ","issue":"The printed full stop interrupts the construction joining μὲν with κατὰ σέ. The translation treats the words as continuous in sense without silently altering the supplied punctuation.","proposed_reading":"καὶ τὰ μὲν κατὰ σὲ","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"7","text":"Let the duties concerning the elders be these: above all, let them quickly join the young in marriage, forestalling the snares of youthful desire. But let them not neglect marriage even for those already old, for in some people desire remains vigorous even after they have grown old. Therefore, so that sexual immorality may not gain ground against you and cast the same plague into your midst, take precautions beforehand and investigate whether the fire of adultery may be springing up secretly among you. For adultery is exceedingly terrible—so much so that it holds second place in punishment, since first place is awarded to those who are in error, even if they are chaste. Therefore, as elders of the church, train Christ’s bride in chastity (and by “bride” I mean the corporate body of the church). For if she is found chaste by the bridegroom king, she will obtain the greatest honor, and you, as those invited to the wedding, will enjoy great rejoicing. But if she is discovered to have sinned, she will be cast out, and you will pay the penalty if perhaps the sin came about through your neglect.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς γάμον ζευγνύτωσαν","chosen":"let them join the young in marriage","rationale":"ζευγνύω literally joins or yokes together and here refers to arranging marriage."},{"source_quote":"τῆς νεαζούσης ἐπιθυμίας τὰ παγιδεύματα","chosen":"the snares of youthful desire","rationale":"The rendering preserves the trapping image of παγίδευμα and treats νεάζουσα as characterizing desire associated with youth."},{"source_quote":"ἡ πορνεία νομὴν λαβοῦσα καθ’ ὑμῶν","chosen":"sexual immorality may not gain ground against you","rationale":"νομὴν λαμβάνειν can describe spreading or gaining range, especially of disease or fire; “gain ground” retains that image."},{"source_quote":"τὰ δευτερεῖα ἔχειν αὐτὴν τῆς κολάσεως","chosen":"it holds second place in punishment","rationale":"δευτερεῖα denotes the second rank or prize; the ranking image is retained."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἐν πλάνῃ οὖσιν","chosen":"those who are in error","rationale":"πλάνη may denote doctrinal or moral error, but the text does not explicitly narrow its reference."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὸ σύστημα","chosen":"the corporate body of the church","rationale":"σύστημα denotes an organized whole or collective body rather than a building."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"8","text":"Therefore, above all, concern yourselves with chastity, for sexual immorality has been decreed exceedingly grave in God’s sight. There are many kinds of sexual immorality, as Clement himself will also explain to you. But the first is adultery: a man’s not having relations only with his own wife, and a woman’s not having relations only with her own husband. If someone is chaste, he can also become benevolent, and for this he will obtain eternal mercy. Just as adultery is a great evil, so benevolence is the greatest good. Therefore love all your brothers with reverent and merciful eyes, doing for orphans what parents do and for widows what husbands do, providing with complete gladness their food, marriages for those in their prime, and, for those among them without a trade, devising through occupations the means of necessary sustenance: work for a craftsperson, mercy for the inactive person.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"παρὰ τῷ θεῷ χαλεπὴ ὥρισται ἡ πορνεία","chosen":"sexual immorality has been decreed grave in God’s sight","rationale":"ὁρίζω indicates authoritative determination, while χαλεπή here describes severity or gravity."},{"source_quote":"πρώτη μοιχεία ἐστὶν","chosen":"the first is adultery","rationale":"πρώτη is understood as the first of the previously mentioned kinds of sexual immorality, without adding “worst.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἄνδρα μὴ ἰδίᾳ μόνῃ χρήσασθαι γυναικὶ","chosen":"a man’s not having relations only with his own wife","rationale":"χρῆσθαι with a spouse in this sexual context denotes marital or sexual relations; a literal “use” would mislead in English."},{"source_quote":"φιλάνθρωπος","chosen":"benevolent","rationale":"The adjective describes humane generosity or care for others."},{"source_quote":"ἡ φιλανθρωπία μέγιστον ἀγαθόν","chosen":"benevolence is the greatest good","rationale":"The noun denotes humane generosity or care and is distinguished from the explicit command ἀγαπᾶτε, rendered “love.”},{"                                                                                                                   
                     }],"source_issues":[]}]}
